title: Jobs, investments, and exporting: the real effects of electricity crisis in South Africa
summary: How South Africa's electricity crises affected manufacturers' jobs, investment and exports, and what that means for an industrial strategy built on a greener grid.
keyFindings: The electricity crises destroyed jobs, lowered capital investment and disrupted exports of manufacturing firms.
The adverse effects are most severe for firms in sectors with higher energy vulnerability.
Ownership structure, firm age and financial status shape how much firms are affected.
methods: Generalised difference-in-differences exploiting sectoral differences in exposure to the electricity crisis (earlier version: WIDER Working Paper 2024/89).
